panels.title: Accounts and agents created (cumulative)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_timestamp(created_at_ms / 1000) AS time,
       entity AS metric,
       count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY entity ORDER BY created_at_ms) AS "created"
FROM metrics.tenancy
WHERE created_at_ms IS NOT NULL
  AND created_at_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
ORDER BY created_at_ms

panels.description: Phone numbers are absent on purpose: the schema records no creation time for them, only a last-modified timestamp, and drawing a curve from an edit would invent history. Their total is the tile above.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_timestamp(day_ms / 1000) AS time,
       sum(inbound_calls) AS "inbound",
       sum(outbound_calls) AS "outbound"
FROM metrics.workspace_daily
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY day_ms
ORDER BY day_ms

SELECT to_timestamp(day_ms / 1000) AS time, sum(minutes) AS "minutes"
FROM metrics.workspace_daily
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY day_ms
ORDER BY day_ms

panels.title: Peak concurrent calls, per hour

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_timestamp(hour_ms / 1000) AS time, max(peak_concurrent) AS "peak"
FROM metrics.concurrency_hourly
WHERE hour_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY hour_ms
ORDER BY hour_ms

panels.description: Overlapping calls, from call start/end times. Prometheus cannot answer this beyond 15 days; the calls table keeps everything. Calls still in flight are excluded — they have no end event.

panels.title: Calls that never connected (excluded from minutes)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_timestamp(day_ms / 1000) AS time,
       sum(unconnected_calls) AS "never connected",
       sum(error_calls) AS "errored"
FROM metrics.workspace_daily
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY day_ms
ORDER BY day_ms

panels.description: Why 'calls' and 'minutes' disagree. A dial that was never answered consumed no audio, so it contributes no minutes — but it is still a call that happened, and hiding it would make the gap look like a bug.

panels.title: LLM turns per day

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_timestamp(day_ms / 1000) AS time, sum(llm_turns) AS "turns"
FROM metrics.workspace_daily
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY day_ms
ORDER BY day_ms

panels.description: Turn counts begin at #261, which fixed realtime sessions recording no latency samples at all. Earlier calls report no turns rather than zero turns; the coverage panel beside this one says how much of the window that affects.

panels.title: Cost per minute

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(total_cost_usd)
       / nullif(sum(CASE WHEN total_cost_usd IS NOT NULL THEN minutes END), 0) AS "cost/min"
FROM metrics.call_cost
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000

panels.description: Variable cost only, and NULL-safe: minutes whose model has no rate row are excluded from both halves rather than counted as free.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(total_cost_usd) AS "cost"
FROM metrics.call_cost
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000

panels.title: Cost and implied margin per day

targets.rawSql:
SELECT to_timestamp(day_ms / 1000) AS time,
       sum(total_cost_usd) AS "cost",
       sum(implied_margin_usd) AS "implied margin"
FROM metrics.call_cost
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY day_ms
ORDER BY day_ms

panels.description: Margin here is IMPLIED, not earned: there is no billing system and nobody is charged. It is what this traffic would have earned at the list price the pricing rule computes. Cost is duration x rate, not metered consumption — a call with an unusually long prompt costs the same here as a quiet one of equal length.

panels.title: Per workspace

targets.rawSql:
WITH window_calls AS (
  SELECT * FROM metrics.call_cost
  WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
), totals AS (
  SELECT sum(minutes) AS all_minutes FROM window_calls
), infra AS (
  -- metrics.fixed_cost, not cost_rates: grafana_ro holds no grant on the rate
  -- tables, and granting one would also hand over the per-minute rates our
  -- margin is derived from.
  SELECT monthly_usd
         * (($__unixEpochTo()::bigint - $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint)::numeric / 86400 / 30)
           AS window_usd
  FROM metrics.fixed_cost
  WHERE component = 'infra_fixed_monthly'
    AND effective_from_ms <= $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
  ORDER BY effective_from_ms DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT c.workspace_id                                              AS "workspace",
       count(*)                                                    AS "calls",
       round(sum(c.minutes)::numeric, 1)                           AS "minutes",
       round(sum(c.total_cost_usd)::numeric, 4)                    AS "variable cost",
       round((i.window_usd * sum(c.minutes) / nullif(t.all_minutes, 0))::numeric, 2)
                                                                   AS "allocated infra",
       round((sum(c.total_cost_usd) / nullif(sum(c.minutes), 0))::numeric, 5)
                                                                   AS "cost/min",
       round(sum(c.implied_margin_usd)::numeric, 4)                AS "implied margin"
FROM window_calls c
CROSS JOIN totals t
CROSS JOIN infra i
GROUP BY c.workspace_id, i.window_usd, t.all_minutes
ORDER BY sum(c.minutes) DESC NULLS LAST

panels.description: Margin here is IMPLIED, not earned: there is no billing system and nobody is charged. It is what this traffic would have earned at the list price the pricing rule computes. Cost is duration x rate, not metered consumption — a call with an unusually long prompt costs the same here as a quiet one of equal length. Fixed infrastructure is allocated by minute share and kept in its own column: folding a fixed cost into a per-minute one produces a number that falls as volume rises and looks like an efficiency gain that is really just division.

panels.title: Spread by model

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(model_id, '(unresolved)')          AS "model",
       rule_source                                 AS "priced by",
       count(*)                                    AS "calls",
       round(sum(minutes)::numeric, 1)             AS "minutes",
       round(avg(cost_per_min)::numeric, 5)        AS "cost/min",
       round(avg(price_per_min)::numeric, 5)       AS "price/min",
       round(sum(implied_margin_usd)::numeric, 4)  AS "implied margin"
FROM metrics.call_cost
WHERE day_ms BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()::bigint * 1000 AND $__unixEpochTo()::bigint * 1000
GROUP BY model_id, rule_source
ORDER BY sum(minutes) DESC NULLS LAST

panels.description: 'priced by' is which pricing rule produced the price — an explicit per-model price, a per-model markup, the global rule, or none at all — so an oddly-priced model shows its cause instead of leaving you to reconstruct it from three tables. A blank cost or price means the model has no rate row: unknown, not free.
